records.name: PlasticThreshold.plastic_salem_family
records.entry_name: The compositum of the two Mahler minimizers: exact measure, conjugate census, house, and minimal product recurrence, with the Bedford-Kim plastic family, Lehmer's polynomial, and the E_m Coxeter bridge
records.doc: Kernel-checked certificates for the multiplicative compositum of the two registered Mahler minimizers — rho, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 (the plastic number: Smyth's nonreciprocal minimum, Siegel's smallest Pisot number) and Q, the real root > 1 of x^4 = x + 1 (the degree-4 entry of the minimal-measure tables) — together with the Bedford-Kim spectral family whose limit rho is, and (new in version 2) the identification of that family with the Coxeter-element spectra of the E_m star trees. Twenty-two compared theorems. The spectral half: (1) for n >= 7 the family chi_n(x) = x^(n+1)(x^3 - x - 1) + (x^3 + x^2 - 1) has a canonical root in [117/100, rho), largest below rho, strictly increasing, tending to rho; (2) every chi_n is strictly positive on [rho, infinity); (3) chi_7 = (x - 1) * L exactly, over any commutative ring, with L Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial; (4) L has a root in [117/100, rho). The compositum half, for the degree-12 minimal polynomial of rho * Q (written out in full in every compared statement): (5) an exclusion witness — a nonreal quartic root z with 1 < |rho * z| < rho * Q; (6) the twelve embedding products ARE the conjugates of rho * Q, both directions; (7) there are exactly twelve of them; (8) rho * Q is an algebraic unit, via an explicit degree-11 cofactor over any commutative ring — the (3, 4, 12) triple in the normal form alpha * beta * gamma = 1; (9) the degree-12 polynomial is not reciprocal (neither its reversal nor the reversal's negation), placing it in the regime of Smyth's theorem; (10) degree multiplicativity — deg minpoly(rho*Q) = deg minpoly(rho) * deg minpoly(Q) = 12; (11) the compositum in sup form Q(rho) join Q(Q) = Q(rho*Q), of degree 12, with the two simple extensions linearly disjoint; (12) the complete unit-circle census — EXACTLY 5 conjugates strictly outside, EXACTLY 7 strictly inside, NONE on the circle, so rho * Q is neither a Pisot nor a Salem number; (13) the house — every conjugate other than rho * Q has modulus strictly below rho * Q; (14) the exact Mahler measure M = rho^2 * Q^2 * psi, where psi is the real root > 1 of psi^4 = psi^3 + 1; (15) the registry bridge — M(X^4 - X - 1) = psi and M(rulerPoly) = (rho * Q)^2 * M(X^4 - X - 1), re-proving in-repo the quantity pinned in registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004; (16) the order-12 Hadamard product recurrence — the termwise product of any solutions of the cubic and quartic shift recurrences satisfies the order-12 recurrence whose characteristic polynomial is exactly the degree-12 polynomial, in any Q-algebra; (17) the annihilator ideal of the product power sequence n |-> (rho * Q)^n is EXACTLY the principal ideal of the degree-12 polynomial — the classical order <= 3 * 4 bound is an equality, forced by the polynomial's kernel-held irreducibility. THE COXETER BRIDGE (version 2), for the star trees E_m = T(2,3,m-3) with generalized Cartan matrix A given entrywise and Coxeter element c = s_0 s_1 ... s_{m-1}, each simple reflection the matrix s_i = 1 - e_i e_i^T A of the geometric representation: (18) for every m >= 4, (X - 1) * charpoly(c) = X^(m-2)(X^3 - X - 1) + (X^3 + X^2 - 1) — the classical E_n Coxeter-polynomial identity (recorded in Gross-Hironaka-McMullen 2009, Section 1, and proved there as Cor. 4.3 for n >= 4), whose right-hand side is chi_{m-3}: the spectral half of this entry IS the E_m Coxeter spectrum; (19) with the E_10 Cartan matrix written out, the Coxeter polynomial of E_10 is Lehmer's polynomial; (20) for every m >= 10 the Coxeter polynomial of E_m has a root lambda_m in [117/100, rho) with no real root above it, the lambda_m strictly increasing and tending to rho; (21) for every m >= 10 the complexified Coxeter element has an eigenvalue lambda in (1, rho) and every complex eigenvalue is unimodular, lambda, or 1/lambda; (22) that lambda dominates the modulus of every eigenvalue and is a Salem number, for every m >= 10, with the Salem predicate written out as in the registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000003. Two disclosures of version 1 are discharged by (21)-(22) for n >= 7: the Salem property of the Bedford-Kim roots is now kernel-held, and the interval (1, 117/100) is now swept (the only eigenvalues off the unit circle are lambda_m and its inverse). The results address four research audiences: the degree problem for products and composita of algebraic numbers (the certified (3,4,12) witness at a canonically distinguished pair, in the field's own unit-product normal form); the Mahler-measure tradition (the measure of the composed product of the two degree-minimal polynomials, in closed form in the second-smallest Pisot number); composed products of polynomials (a certified rational instance where the finite-field coprimality criterion is unavailable and irreducibility is proved by elimination); and, new, Coxeter groups and Salem numbers (McMullen; Gross-Hironaka-McMullen; Hironaka's Lehmer program): the E_m Coxeter spectra, their Salem radii and their limit rho as one kernel-checked family — with the Lean audience served by concrete exercise of the Mahler-measure, linear-disjointness, Matrix.charpoly and spectrum APIs. Like the golden ratio, rho * Q is an algebraic unit of norm -1; the compared cofactor identity is that norm computation, certified. No novelty claim is made for the measure identity (the entry is not aware of it in the literature; the claimed contribution is the kernel certificate), none for the mathematics of (18)-(22), which is classical (the claimed contribution is the kernel-checked bridge from the registered Bedford-Kim family to the E_m Coxeter elements, for every m >= 4 (bridge) and every m >= 10 (spectrum, Salem) at once), no "first formalization" claim is made anywhere, and whether rho is ATTAINED as a dynamical degree is open in the literature — no statement claims it. Hypotheses are inline: rho, Q, psi enter only through their defining equations plus root-selection inequalities, the E_m Cartan matrices only through their entries, and the compared statements use only core Mathlib vocabulary (Filter.Tendsto, nhds, the complex norm, minpoly, Polynomial.rootSet, Set.ncard, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, IntermediateField adjoin/sup, Module.finrank, Finset.range sums, Matrix.charpoly, Matrix.diagonal, List.finRange/List.prod, matrix literals, Matrix.map, spectrum, IsIntegral, Polynomial.aeval) — zero custom definitions. The name prefix "ruler" in statement names is the source project's term for the product rho * Q; nothing in any statement depends on it.

records.name: UnrestrictedBooleanMul.mc_mul_zero
records.entry_name: Unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term polynomial multiplication
records.doc: Formalizes the exact minimum AND-gate counts 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9 for binary polynomial multiplication with zero through four coefficients per operand. XOR and constants are free, and AND inputs may reuse arbitrary earlier nonlinear wires. The principal result excludes eight-gate four-term circuits and matches an explicit nine-gate construction. Separate research workflows check selected n5 quadratic results and n6 upper bounds and reductions; their open unrestricted/bilinear lower bounds are not claims of this submission.

records.entry_name: Formalization of a discrete Carleson theorem of Stein-Wainger type
records.doc: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of the papers arXiv:1907.00405 and arXiv:2107.14616 by Ben Krause and Joris Roos. The result concerns l^p boundedness for a  discrete maximal singular oscillatory operator of Stein-Wainger type, also called a discrete Carleson operator.

records.name: anisotropic_carleson
records.entry_name: Formalization of Carleson's theorem via the Lacey-Thiele approach
records.doc: This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorem 1.1 from the paper "Bounds for anisotropic Carleson operators" by J. Roos, which generalizes the Lacey-Thiele proof for Carleson's theorem. The classical Carleson theorem on pointwise almost everywhere convergence of Fourier series is derived as a special case.

records.name: PalomarSMC.mathematical_result
records.entry_name: Pure infinitely self-modifying code
records.doc: Formalizes the corrected construction of pure infinitely self-modifying code from Gregory Morse's 2018 paper. An unbounded integer-address machine simulates finite Turing machines, preserves halting and divergence, writes code at every computational instruction, and admits a run changing unboundedly many fetched code fields from a literal identity-memory initializer whose memory is proved primitive recursive. Terminal interpreter journals occur on reached halted configurations of the numbered interpreter on the encoded finite input. The development includes a four-register MOV foundation, effective finite-machine interpretation, tape and head observations, and conditional bounded x86/x64 instruction, relocation and native-trace refinements. Finite hardware is not claimed to have unbounded memory.

records.name: PalomarWE.mathematical_result
records.entry_name: Write-Execute Computation and Self-Spectre
records.doc: Formalizes Gregory Morse's 2019 paper "Self-Spectre, Write-Execute and the Hidden State": the Write-Execute half unconditionally, the Self-Spectre half as conditional theorems over an abstract speculation contract. An ideal word-level machine whose only operations are a store and a jump, with no data reads, simulates finite Turing machines step for step, preserving halting, divergence and the tape; a finite image is exact until its guard faults. The development proves the jump-table lookup, the 8-bit tables, wide ADD, SUB, SHL, SHR, XOR, 32x32 multiplication, 64/32 division, two-step modular reduction, modular exponentiation with its multiplication count, the AES-128 T-table cipher and the Write-Execute AES procedure against FIPS-197. The Self-Spectre half is proved as a conditional result under an abstract speculation contract (a branch predictor and a speculation window as parameters, rollback of the architectural state, persistence of the cache): the Fig. 1 mistraining schedule, the Fig. 2 victim leak with the mix-order reload from a cleared probe array, the speculation-depth boundary (touch trace for any cache, observable reload hits from a cleared probe array) and the hidden Write-Execute computation. Supporting byte-level x86/x64 models of Figs. 5, 6 and 7 and native vectors for the corrected C and MASM sources accompany the selected statement.

records.name: PDTSourceSelection.quadraticSelection
records.entry_name: Selection of the electromagnetic source tensor by covariance, conservation and the exchange law
records.doc: On a fixed flat Lorentz frame with metric diag(1,1,1,-1), sources are symmetric 4x4 tensor-valued functions of the six real components of an antisymmetric field. Twelve kernel-checked statements. Among all symmetric homogeneous quadratic sources (210 free coefficients), the six infinitesimal Lorentz covariance equations together with zero trace select the Maxwell stress (the electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor) up to a unique real scale, and a displayed certificate of 209 linear coefficient equations is equivalent to both laws. Among the same homogeneous quadratic sources, conservation alone - vanishing divergence on every source-free Maxwell/Bianchi first jet - selects the same line, with covariance, trace zero and Hodge invariance derived rather than assumed. The globally C^3 symmetric conserved sources are exactly an explicit seventeen-parameter family (constant, a six-parameter cross term, and the stress), and with covariance zero field value is equivalent to zero trace and to the stress line. Under the sourceful exchange law at current stiffness k (the real factor multiplying the jet current), every everywhere-differentiable symmetric source is a constant plus the Maxwell stress of scale exactly k, and conversely, with no polynomial, degree, C^3, covariance or trace hypothesis; zero field value selects the stress. Explicit counterexamples show that covariance and zero trace are each necessary in the quadratic selection, and that covariance and the zero-field normalization are each necessary in the C^3 selection. Uniqueness of the Maxwell stress tensor is classical (Fock 1964; Kerrighan 1982; Navarro-Sancho 2012; the classification of Maxwell conservation laws by Anco-Pohjanpelto 2001); the contribution is the constructive, kernel-checked development on the explicit register at finite regularity, with finite certificates, the covariance-free routes, and the differentiable-only sourceful statement. Pisot Dimensional Theory motivates the frame; no physical coupling is selected.

records.name: Palomar.garding
records.entry_name: Solvability of divergence-form elliptic equations (Evans §6.2)
records.doc:
A Lean 4 formalisation of the solvability theory of linear second-order elliptic operators in divergence form on a bounded domain,

  -div(A grad u) + b · grad u + c u = f in Ω,   u = 0 on ∂Ω,

with A uniformly elliptic and every coefficient bounded and measurable. The drift b is unrestricted and the bilinear form is in general non-symmetric. The six compared statements are the results of Evans §6.2: the Gårding inequality, existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with no drift and a nonnegative zeroth-order coefficient, the Fredholm alternative, solvability against the transpose problem, the discrete set of exceptional shifts and boundedness of the inverse. They ask only that Ω be bounded and open, and the compact embedding of H_0^1(Ω) in L²(Ω) is proved. Interior regularity at every order, the maximum principles and the Dirichlet eigenvalue sequence are also proved in the library and appear without a Comparator configuration. Built on Mathlib with only Lean's standard axioms.

records.name: MengerTheorem.card_le_of_separates
records.entry_name: Menger's theorem, Hamiltonian cycles, long cycles and pancyclicity
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Menger's theorem for finite graphs (set form with a minimum separator and as many vertex-disjoint paths, two-vertex form, edge form for Mathlib's IsEdgeReachable, and the global edge form for Mathlib's IsEdgeConnected) and of classical sufficient conditions for Hamiltonian cycles: the Bondy–Chvátal closure step, Ore's and Dirac's theorems, and the Chvátal–Erdős theorem (k-connected with independence number at most k implies Hamiltonian), whose proof uses Menger's theorem through the fan lemma. Version 2 adds the Erdős–Gallai theorems on long paths and cycles (no path on k vertices implies 2e ≤ (k − 2)n; no cycle of length at least k ≥ 3 implies 2e ≤ (k − 1)(n − 1)) and Bondy's pancyclicity theorem (a Hamiltonian graph with at least n²/4 edges is pancyclic or is K_{n/2,n/2}), proved on top of the same library.

records.name: BrooksColouring.colorable_of_cliqueFree
records.entry_name: Brooks' theorem, degree-choosability and blocks
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Brooks' theorem: for k ≥ 3, a finite graph of maximum degree at most k without a (k+1)-clique is k-colourable (no connectedness assumption), and a finite connected graph that is neither complete nor an odd cycle is colourable with as many colours as its maximum degree. The proof uses greedy colourings in Lovász's style and an induction on the number of edges with a separation-and-gluing step. Version 2 adds the Erdős–Rubin–Taylor / Borodin theorem (a finite connected graph is degree-choosable, i.e. colourable from any lists with |L(v)| ≥ deg(v), if and only if it is not a Gallai tree: some block is neither complete nor an odd cycle), Brooks' theorem for lists (Vizing 1976), and a library of blocks of graphs (blocks as maximal nonseparable vertex sets, cut vertices, unique block per edge, blocks meeting in at most one vertex, the block–cut tree of a connected graph, and the agreement of the block and induced-subgraph descriptions of Gallai trees).

records.name: Superorthogonal.CDW.sqfct_estimate_of_superorthogonal
records.entry_name: Formalization of a sharp cone square-function estimate via superorthogonality
records.doc:
This is a Lean 4 formalization of Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 from the paper "Diameter-free reverse inequalities and superorthogonality" by A. Cushman, C. Demeter and S. Wu.
Theorem 1.1 is a reverse square-function estimate in L^4 under a superorthogonality hypothesis that is weaker than the Type IV superorthogonality of Gressman-Pierce-Roos-Yung.
Theorem 1.4 applies a similar estimate to the three-dimensional light cone, yielding a refinement of the reverse cone square-function estimate of Guth-Wang-Zhang.

records.name: ContinuumIndependence.independence_of_CH
records.entry_name: Continuum hypothesis independence: a Flypitch reproduction
records.doc: An attributed adaptation of the Flypitch formal proof of two-sided syntactic independence of the continuum hypothesis from its explicitly encoded first-order ZFC theory. Cohen and collapse Boolean-valued models, together with soundness, establish that neither the encoded CH sentence nor its negation is derivable. The development uses an expanded language with definable set operations, collection and Zorn's lemma. It does not supply a formal translation to membership-only ZFC or determine the truth of CH for the ambient Lean reals. This is a reproduction of established work, not a new mathematical solution.

records.name: RestrictedSumsetsAudit.counterexample_main
records.entry_name: Counterexamples to the restricted-sumset inverse theorem in arXiv:2609.10148v2
records.doc: Explicit finite counterexamples to Theorem A (Theorem 3.1) and Lemma 3.2 of Li and Liang, arXiv:2609.10148v2. In Z/13Z, sets of sizes seven and four satisfy all size hypotheses and have restricted sumset size nine, but neither is an arithmetic progression. A separate example in Z/11Z contradicts the lower bound of Lemma 3.2 as stated.

records.name: ModalDepth.Contracts.uniform_classification
records.entry_name: Depth-labeled interpolation and substitution in Sacchetti's modal logics
records.doc: Classifies depth labelings in the modal logics wGL_n for positive n. Every simultaneous formula-valued substitution indexed by atom and depth label preserves theoremhood exactly when the labels satisfy c(k+n)=c(k) at every positive depth k. The interpolation equivalences identify the corresponding labeled property with its ordinary interpolation property and the same periodicity condition; the ordinary interpolation theorems remain explicit inputs. Further results classify period spectra, boxed-atom implications and composition of depth substitutions, and transfer a supplied ordinary interpolant while preserving syntax-tree node count and modal depth.

records.name: Erdos99.erdos99_finite_multiplicity
records.entry_name: Erdos 99 Partial Solution
records.doc: A formalization of a partial solution to Erdos Problem 99. It shows that Erdos Problem 99 holds for all sufficiently large n where h(n) is finite. Here, h(n) denotes the number of incongruence, diameter-minimizing sets of minimum separation at least 1.

records.name: BergeTheorem.isMaximum_iff_not_exists_augmenting
records.entry_name: Berge's theorem, the Tutte–Berge formula and the Gallai–Edmonds theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Berge's augmenting path theorem (a matching is maximum if and only if there is no augmenting path) and of the Tutte–Berge formula (the maximum size of a matching is the minimum over vertex sets U of (|V| + |U| − odd(G − U)) / 2), with the weak inequality for all matchings and vertex sets; the formula is derived from Mathlib's Tutte theorem by adding universal vertices. Version 2 adds the Gallai–Edmonds structure theorem: with D the vertices missed by some maximum matching, A their neighbours outside D and C the rest, the components of G[D] are factor-critical, G[C] has a perfect matching, every maximum matching matches A into distinct components of G[D], and 2ν(G) = |V| + |A| − c(G[D]).

records.name: KKP.connected_counterexample_family
records.entry_name: Connected counterexamples to the exact color-critical two-eigenvalue bound
records.doc: For F=K5 minus one edge, a color-critical graph of chromatic number four, the graph formed from K(s,s,s) and K4 by one bridge is connected and F-free for every integer s at least three. It has 3s squared plus 7 edges, and the sum of squares of its two largest ordered adjacency eigenvalues exceeds 4m/3 by at least (656s squared-1366s+62)/(3(37s-1) squared)>0. The family has arbitrarily large edge counts, refuting the exact assertion in KKP Conjecture 1.16 and Li–Liu–Zhang Conjecture 5.4.

records.name: Glennie.SubmissionR03.q26_eq_iff_fullLedger_eq
records.entry_name: Finite Observations and Recognition of the Compact Albert Algebra
records.doc:

A frame p=(p_0,p_1,p_2) consists of trace-one elements satisfying p_i∘p_i=p_i, p_i∘p_j=0 for i≠j, and p_0+p_1+p_2=1. For frames p,q,r, record the 27 pair traces T(p_i∘q_j), T(q_j∘r_k), T(r_k∘p_i), and 27 triple traces T((p_i∘q_j)∘r_k), for i,j,k∈{0,1,2}. How much do these traces determine?

Each trace list in some open neighborhood of the data with pair entries 1/3 and triple entries 1/9, in a fixed twenty-dimensional chart, determines exactly two equivalence classes. Equivalence means one product-and-trace-preserving real linear bijection acting on all nine labeled elements, without relabeling. The sign of the degree-nine scalar Phi distinguishes the classes. With x=p_2−p_0, y=q_2−q_0, z=r_2−r_0, define

B(a,b) = T(a∘b),
U_a(b) = 2a∘(a∘b)−(a∘a)∘b,
Phi(x,y,z) = B((U_x U_y−U_y U_x)z,U_z(x∘y)).

Phi's derivative uses Glennie's degree-eight vector polynomial.

For arbitrary x,y,z∈J, Phi≠0 implies that 1,x,y,z generate J.

Recognition starts from a homogeneous cubic N on finite-dimensional real normed E, with N(e)=1 and g_e=−(1/3)D²(log N)_e positive definite on all E. A supplied linear equivalence ker(DN_e)≃ker T (the trace-zero subspace), matching g_e to B/3 and full vector-valued curvature tensors, yields an Albert algebra equivalence.

Consider 27 fixed parenthesized products of a distinguished element and three chosen elements in a real inner-product space with bilinear multiplication. Exact matching with the Albert table of pairwise inner products, inner products of products with these expressions and full ambient squared product norms determines a unique isometric, product-preserving linear embedding of J onto the subspace they generate under products and linear combinations, preserving the distinguished element and chosen elements.

Further results give error bounds. All project exposition and Lean code are AI-generated under Robert MacGregor's direction. Robert is a non-mathematician and welcomes mathematical collaboration: macgregor@gmail.com. No novelty is asserted.

records.name: QuantumDesigns.hasMUBs_le
records.entry_name: Finite quantum designs: mutually unbiased bases, SIC-POVMs, and the Welch and Gerzon bounds
records.doc: A Lean 4 development of two structures of finite-dimensional quantum information, in the vocabulary of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (Open Quantum Problems 13 and 23; the fourteen definitions restated character for character under their Apache-2.0 license, see NOTICE). A basis of C^d is a unitary matrix whose columns are the basis vectors; two bases U, V are mutually unbiased when every entry of U^* V has squared norm 1/d; HasMUBs d k says k pairwise unbiased bases exist and IsMaxMUBCount d k that k is the largest such number. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.

Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. As of 2026-10-10 no formalization of the general bound, of the prime-power constructions, of the factorization corollary, of the complex absolute bound with its equality case, of Weiner's gap for general d, of Welch's bound, of the two reconstruction formulas for every matrix or of a SIC-POVM in dimension 4 was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib, the other Lean repositories searched, the Isabelle AFP, the Rocq package index or arXiv; none of the second moment of a SIC family with its norm, distance and purity forms, of Welch's deficit with its equality case, of the equality case of the relative bound, of the SIC family from d^2 vectors at or below the SIC angle or of the frame-defect bound was located in the Palomar registry, Mathlib, formal-conjectures, openai/math, physlib or the-omega-institute/trureturing. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.

Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system. Not claimed: anything about dimension 6 beyond 3 <= mu(6) <= 7 and mu(6) != 6 (openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5), SICs in dimensions 5 to 7, that a family near the SIC angle is close to a SIC family, any first formalization.

Theorems: for d >= 2, HasMUBs d m implies m <= d + 1 (Wootters-Fields 1989; Bandyopadhyay-Boykin-Roychowdhury-Vatan 2002, Theorem 3.5: the identity and the m(d - 1) traceless combinations of the rank-one projectors are pairwise orthogonal in the d^2-dimensional matrix space), and the hypothesis is sharp since in dimension 1 every two bases are unbiased; restriction to subfamilies; the tensor bound HasMUBs m k and HasMUBs n k imply HasMUBs (m n) k (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2004, Lemma 3) and its corollary over the factorization (HasMUBs d k whenever k <= q + 1 for every exact prime-power divisor q of d), hence three mutually unbiased bases in every dimension d >= 2; for a finite field F of odd characteristic and size q, the standard basis and the q bases with entries psi(a x^2 + b x)/sqrt q (psi a nontrivial additive character) are q + 1 mutually unbiased bases (Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 2), through the identity |sum_x psi(c x^2 + e x)|^2 = q for c != 0 proved by Weyl differencing; for q = 2^n the bases with entries i^(x^T S_a x) (-1)^(b . x)/sqrt q, S_a the {0, 1}-lifted Gram matrix of the trace form (x, y) -> Tr(a x y) of the field with 2^n elements (an equivalent form of the Galois-ring bases of Klappenecker-Rötteler, Theorem 3), through the mod-4 identity Q(x + y) = Q(x) + Q(y) + 2 x^T S y and the nondegeneracy of the trace form; so IsMaxMUBCount (p^k) (p^k + 1) for every prime power, HasCompleteMUBs d iff IsMaxMUBCount d (d + 1) for d >= 2, and the values 3, 5, 9 in dimensions 2, 4, 8 also by explicit kernel-checked tables. Weiner's gap (Weiner 2013, Corollary 3.4): any d mutually unbiased bases of C^d extend, by one more basis, to a complete set of d + 1, the given bases keeping their places, for every d (and in the existence form, HasMUBs d d implies HasCompleteMUBs d), by Weiner's proof with its operator-algebra steps written out. The orthogonal projection Phi onto the matrices with a constant diagonal in every one of the d bases has a Kraus form X -> sum_i K_i^* X K_i whose operators K_i have constant diagonals themselves (Weiner's Lemma 3.2, through his Lemma 2.1, sum_k A_k^* X A_k = Tr(X) 1 for an orthonormal basis A_k of the matrix space, recalled there from Werner 2001); at a fixed point X the Kadison-Schwarz defect sum_i K_i^* X^* X K_i - Phi(X)^* Phi(X) is the sum of the squares (X K_i - K_i X)^* (X K_i - K_i X) and has zero trace, so the K_i commute with one another and with their adjoints (in place of the Schwarz inequality and the multiplicative-domain theorem of Choi 1974 that the paper's Lemma 3.1 uses); and the rank-one projectors of a common eigenbasis of the K_i are fixed by Phi, hence have constant diagonals, hence are unbiased to every basis of the family. Corollaries: k >= d bases give a complete set; for d >= 2, d is never the maximal number (in particular mu(6) != 6), and the maximal number is d + 1 or below d. The maximal number mu(d): two bases in every dimension; HasMUBs (p^k) m iff m <= p^k + 1; mu(d) is unique, exists for d >= 2 and lies in [3, d + 1], and does not exist for d = 1; formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim6_bounds, 3 <= mu(6) <= 7, left with sorry there. Reconstruction (Scott 2006, eq. (9)): a complete set of d + 1 bases determines every matrix, X = sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) P_{s,l} - Tr(X) 1 with P_{s,l} the projector onto column l of basis s (after Ivanović 1981 and Wootters-Fields 1989), and so does a SIC family, X = sum_i ((d + 1) Tr(X P_i) - Tr X)/d P_i (its projectors are linearly independent, Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, section II). Second moments (Klappenecker-Rötteler 2005, Theorems 3 and 5; Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004, p. 4; Scott 2006, eq. (8)): for all matrices X, Y, sum_{s,l} Tr(X P_{s,l}) Tr(Y P_{s,l}) = Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y for a complete set and (d + 1) sum_i Tr(X P_i) Tr(Y P_i) = d (Tr(XY) + Tr X Tr Y) for a SIC family; hence the data Tr(X P_{s,l}), and the SIC-POVM outcomes Tr(X P_i)/d with the factor d(d + 1), give ||X||_HS^2 + |Tr X|^2, the Hilbert-Schmidt distance of two matrices with equal traces, and the purity Tr(rho^2) of a Hermitian rho with Tr rho = 1 (Larsen 1990, not read, as stated by Wu-Yu-Mølmer 2009; Scott 2006, eqs. (32), (36), (55)). A SIC family in C^d is d^2 unit vectors with pairwise squared overlap 1/(d + 1); HasSICPOVM d says one exists. Theorems: N unit vectors of C^d with one squared overlap c != 1 on every pair satisfy N <= d^2 (the absolute bound of Delsarte-Goethals-Seidel 1975, the complex form of Gerzon's bound; the rank-one projectors are linearly independent), and with c = 1 the family may be any length; for d >= 2, d^2 such vectors have c = 1/(d + 1) and resolve the identity, sum_i (1/d) |phi_i><phi_i| = 1, so every SIC family is a POVM (Renes-Blume-Kohout-Scott-Caves 2004), HasSICPOVM d holds iff C^d has d^2 equiangular unit vectors, and a family at the SIC angle has at most d^2 members; Welch's bound (Welch 1974, the bound for k = 1, in the frame-potential form of Benedetto-Fickus 2003): N unit vectors of C^d have sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 >= N^2/d, by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the identity and the frame operator in the matrix space; hence N >= 2 unit vectors with one squared overlap c on every pair have c >= (N - d)/(d (N - 1)), pairwise squared overlaps at most alpha with alpha d < 1 give N (1 - alpha d) <= d (1 - alpha) (the relative bound), and at most d^2 unit vectors have every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1). Welch's equality case (Mixon-Needham-Shonkwiler-Villar, Proposition 1 and its proof): sum_{i,j} |<phi_i, phi_j>|^2 - N^2/d = ||S - (N/d) 1||_HS^2 for the frame operator S = sum_i |phi_i><phi_i|, so equality holds exactly for a tight frame; at equality in the relative bound every pairwise squared overlap is alpha and S = (N/d) 1 (Strohmer-Heath 2003, Theorem 2.3); d^2 unit vectors with every pairwise squared overlap at most 1/(d + 1) are a SIC family, and HasSICPOVM d holds iff such vectors exist; and pairwise squared overlaps at most 1/(d + 1) + epsilon give ||S/d - 1||_HS^2 <= (d^2 - 1) epsilon for d >= 1, a bound on the resolution of the identity only. SIC-POVMs exist in dimensions 2 (the tetrahedron), 3 (the Hesse configuration), 4 (the sixteen Weyl-Heisenberg translates of Appleby's exact fiducial, Appleby 2005, eq. (149), credited there to Zauner and to Renes et al.; covariance reduces the 240 overlaps to fifteen, proved by exact trigonometric and radical identities in cos(pi/8), sin(pi/8) and sqrt(2 + sqrt 5)) and 8 (Hoggar's 64 lines: the orbit of (-1 + 2i, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)/sqrt 12 under the three-qubit Pauli group, Jedwab-Wiebe 2015, Example 4, checked by the kernel over all ordered pairs). Sixty compared statements, kernel-only. Read 2026-10-14, after that search: marozols/SIC-existence (public 2026-10-09, Lean v4.34.1, self-assessed, unregistered) states SICs in every dimension and, in RSIC.lean, the N = d^2 equality case, in its own vocabulary, so a dimension-4 SIC and that equality case exist elsewhere in Lean; the statements here are over formal-conjectures' definitions and were proved independently. The neighbours: the dimension-2 MUB case is formal-conjectures' mutuallyUnbiasedBases_dim2; the dimension-6 projector bound and the Kronecker lemma are in the XC0R fork of formal-conjectures (adapted here, see NOTICE); the dimension-2 and 3 SIC overlaps are in zblore/csd-lean4; the-omega-institute/trureturing kernel-checks the same 64 Hoggar vectors and the Hesse SIC in its own vocabulary, proves that the trace pairings with a complete family of rank-one contexts determine every matrix, proves the density-matrix formula under an assumed completeness hypothesis, and proves the second moment of a complete set in operator form with the purity identity for density matrices (complete_context_collision_conservation, 2026-08-28); openai/math holds mu(6) <= 5 and Weiner's gap at d = 6 (six_extend_to_seven), with lemmas for general n (commutator_trace_identity, commute_of_kraus_fixed, exists_joint_projection_basis) that make the same elementary move as the route here, the Schwarz defect of a Kraus map as a sum of squared commutators; the Kadison-Schwarz inequality for Kraus and completely positive maps is in physlib, QuAIR/Lean-QIT and kencyke/quantum-system.
