records.name: LeanLab.PNTPort.PsiChi.siegelWalfisz
records.entry_name: Vinogradov's three primes theorem and almost all binary Goldbach, after Heath-Brown 1985, with the Siegel-Walfisz theorem
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of the main results of D. R. Heath-Brown, The ternary Goldbach problem, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 1 (1985): the Siegel-Walfisz theorem in the form the paper quotes as (1.1), proved from a zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions and Siegel's theorem; Theorem 1, sum over 2x < m <= 3x of |N2(m) - x S(m)| << x^2 (log x)^{-C}; Corollary 1 and the van der Corput, Chudakov, Estermann theorem that at most O(X (log X)^{-A}) even numbers up to X are not sums of two primes, and density zero; Corollary 2, Vinogradov's theorem that every sufficiently large odd number is a sum of three primes; and Corollary 3, infinitely many three-term arithmetic progressions of primes. All constants are ineffective, as in the paper. Binary Goldbach is not claimed. records.name: PalomarKakeya.upperMinkowski_lower
records.entry_name: Two-scale Kakeya upper Minkowski lower bound
records.doc: We prove that every bounded Kakeya set in Rⁿ, n ≥ 4, has upper Minkowski dimension at least 0.597n. Here a Kakeya set contains a unit line segment in every direction. This improves the asymptotic coefficient c_KT = 1/α = 0.596968283237… in the Katz–Tao bound 1 + c_KT(n−1), where α is the unique root of α³−4α+2 = 0 in (1,2). The proof combines arithmetic estimates for line segments with geometric estimates for tubes at two different widths.

records.name: PerfectGraphTheorem.isPerfect_iff_card_le
records.entry_name: Lovász's perfect graph theorems
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Lovász's 1972 theorems on perfect graphs: a finite simple graph is perfect (every induced subgraph has chromatic number equal to its clique number) if and only if |S| ≤ α(G[S]) · ω(G[S]) for every vertex set S; and the perfect graph theorem conjectured by Berge, that a finite graph is perfect if and only if its complement is perfect. The proof follows Gasparian's linear-algebra argument. Mathlib has chromatic, clique and independence numbers but no perfect graphs.

records.name: LewkoDensityPalomar.provider_P1
records.entry_name: Improved zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function
records.doc: We establish improved zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function relative to the bounds previously released in PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000010 v1 and PALOMAR-2026-10-09-000005 v1. Let N(σ,T) count the nontrivial zeros with Re ρ ≥ σ and |Im ρ| ≤ T, with analytic multiplicity. For T ≥ 2 and ε > 0, our bounds have the form N(σ,T) ≤ C(σ,ε)T^((1−σ)A(σ)+ε). The native quantitative bounds improve those earlier power curves for 12/17 < σ ≤ 3/4 and 7/9 < σ ≤ 7/8. The displayed power-curve comparison continues for 7/8 < σ < 17/19, where the imported OpenAI result already gives N(σ,T)=0. Later Lean-formalized refinements also give a zero-free region below 7/8 [Collet26]; our comparisons near 7/8 concern the named earlier results. Table 1 gives all the proved contribution curves and their full ranges, including A(σ)=12/(9σ−1) on [5/7,113/153] and A(σ)=255/(153σ+7) on [113/153,3/4]. Figure 1 compares the cumulative curves.

records.doc: We establish improved zero-density estimates for the Riemann zeta function relative to the bounds previously released in PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000010 v1 and PALOMAR-2026-10-09-000005 v1. Let N(σ,T) count the nontrivial zeros with Re ρ ≥ σ and |Im ρ| ≤ T, with analytic multiplicity. For T ≥ 2 and ε > 0, our bounds have the form N(σ,T) ≤ C(σ,ε)T^((1−σ)A(σ)+ε). The native quantitative bounds improve those earlier power curves for 12/17 < σ ≤ 3/4 and 7/9 < σ ≤ 7/8. The displayed power-curve comparison continues for 7/8 < σ < 17/19, where the imported OpenAI result already gives N(σ,T)=0. Later Lean-formalized refinements also give a zero-free region below 7/8 [Collet26]; our comparisons near 7/8 concern the named earlier results. Table 1 gives all the proved contribution curves and their full ranges, including A(σ)=12/(9σ−1) on [5/7,113/153] and A(σ)=255/(153σ+7) on [113/153,3/4]. Figure 1 compares the cumulative curves.

records.name: NashWilliamsTheorem.nash_williams
records.entry_name: The Nash–Williams triangle-decomposition theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the Nash–Williams theorem for large graphs proved by Delcourt and Postle: there is N such that every finite simple graph on n ≥ N vertices that is triangle-divisible (3 divides the number of edges and every degree is even) and has minimum degree at least 3n/4 has a triangle decomposition; together with Delcourt–Postle's fractional threshold (every graph with 3n ≤ 4δ has a fractional triangle decomposition) and their fractional stability theorem (with an additional order threshold). The proof follows their extremal/non-extremal case division but does not assume their Theorem 13.16, whose proof is assigned to an unpublished manuscript: the extremal residuals are decomposed with typed absorption results developed in the same project, and the non-extremal case with a protected covering-round argument. The development has 1,070 modules.

records.name: P161Formal.template_free_heredity_finite_stock
records.entry_name: Chemical heredity without genetic templates
records.doc: Acquisition and retention of catalytic function are established for a four-compartment chemical model with three prescribed catalyst types and finite resources. Starting with at least 512 copies of each of two old catalyst types per compartment, arbitrary candidate counts and arbitrary fuel occupancy, a seeding phase ends at time 30. At the fixed beta = 4,000,000 operating point, the joint mission through time 60 has failure probability at most 0.004517975690072193. records.name: LeanLab.GoldbachAverage.avgRH_of_RH
records.entry_name: The Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to an asymptotic for the average number of Goldbach representations, after Granville 2007
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1A of A. Granville, Refinements of Goldbach's conjecture, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis, Funct. Approx. Comment. Math. 37 (2007): with G(n) the sum over m1 + m2 = n of Lambda(m1) Lambda(m2), Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis holds if and only if the sum of G(n) over n <= N is N^2/2 + O(N^{3/2+eps}) for every eps > 0. Both directions are proved with no hypothesis: RH implies the asymptotic through the von Koch bound for psi(x) - x, and the asymptotic implies RH by the route reconstructed in part by Bhowmik, Halupczok, Matsumoto, Suzuki (arXiv 1704.06103) and completed by Bhowmik and Ruzsa (arXiv 1711.06442). Binary Goldbach is not claimed. Lean code written by an AI agent; the statements were checked against the literature by an AI reviewer and are offered for human audit.

records.name: HermiteSignatureCompositum.hermite_signature
records.entry_name: Hermite's signature theorem and the coprime compositum, with the degree-12 compositum of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
records.doc:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six general theorems and twelve statements about one number field. General: (1) Hermite's signature theorem for every real polynomial f, degenerate case included and with no monic hypothesis: the power-sum Hankel (Hermite) form H_f has sigPos = #R + #C+, sigNeg = #C+, rank sigPos + sigNeg = #D and radical of dimension deg f - #D, where D, R, C+ are the distinct complex roots, the real ones, and those in the upper half plane; (2) its number-field form (classical, Hermite-Sylvester; in number-field form credited to O. Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). The field: the compositum L of Q(rho) and Q(Q), rho and Q roots of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1, built as the tower K3 = Q[X]/(X^3 - X - 1), L = K3[Y]/(Y^4 - Y - 1), of degree 12: (7) the setting (degrees 3, 4, 12; linearly disjoint sectors); (8) O_{Q(rho)} = Z[rho], O_{Q(Q)} = Z[Q], discriminants -23 and -283, O_L = Z[rho, Q] with basis rho^i Q^j; (9) d_L = (-23)^4 (-283)^3 = -6342648595267; (10) places (1,1), (2,1), (2,5) and the trace-form type (7,5) of L, derived from (2) and (3) with no root located; (11) the relative traces on the product basis; (12) Tr(-alpha^-1) = 1 for alpha^n = alpha + 1 in degree n, the unit sections -Q^-1 and -rho^-1 of the relative traces, their surjectivity on rings of integers and the integral splittings of ranks 3 + 9 and 4 + 8; (13) the orthogonal decompositions of L along the two sectors, with restrictions 4 Tr and 3 Tr of types (2,1), (3,1) and complements of types (5,4), (4,4); (14) the covolume 2^-5 23^2 283 sqrt(283) of O_L in Mathlib's normalization, which is 4 times the product covol(O_{Q(rho)})^4 covol(O_{Q(Q)})^3; (15) the discriminant -23^4 53^2 283^3 of the degree-12 polynomial, which is the minimal polynomial of rho Q, and the index [O_L : Z[rho Q]] = 53; (16) the subfield lattice {Q, Q(rho), Q(Q), L}; (17) root-rigidity and circle-freeness of L; (18) Smyth's lower bound for the Mahler measure on O_L, with Smyth's theorem as an explicit hypothesis (cited, not proved). Eighteen compared theorems. The mathematics of (1)-(6) is classical and no novelty is claimed for it; the contribution is the kernel-checked proofs: (1), (2) and (5) from Mathlib's sigPos, sigNeg (D. Loeffler) and, for (2) and (5), Algebra.traceForm, between which Mathlib has no theorem at the pinned revision; (3) and (4) from Mathlib's infinite places and linear disjointness. The proof modules also prove, not compared, that sigPos and sigNeg are additive over orthogonal direct sums and invariant under positive scaling over any linearly ordered field, and that the signature of a rational matrix form is unchanged by base change to R; Mathlib at the pin has none of these. Mathlib prior art is used and not re-proved: X. Roblot's theorem on the absolute value of the discriminant of a coprime compositum (statement (4) adds the sign) and his theorem on its ring of integers (used in (8)). The definiteness corollary of (1) (real-rooted iff H_f positive semidefinite) was formalized in Lean 4 by P. Alexandersson (RealRooted, 2026-09-27) before this entry; (1) proves the full rank/signature/radical count, from which that corollary follows. No prior formalization of the rank and signature count of the Hermite form, or of the trace-form signature (r1 + r2, r2) of a number field, was found by a search on 2026-10-19 (Mathlib, the Isabelle AFP, Coq/MathComp, HOL Light, Lean 4 community repositories, Zenodo, arXiv); the existing root-counting formalizations use sign variations of remainder sequences. The sector inputs of the field at the level of Q are ported from the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 and are not compared; (7) and the minimal-polynomial clause of (15) re-prove facts certified in the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005 and are not new. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K is the parent of both. Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

Read through the theory, this entry's theorems make six conclusions exact.
Space and spacetime are the only worlds the parent contains. The fields between Q and K have degrees 3 and 4 and no others: Q(rho) and Q(Q) are K's only proper subfields other than Q (16). An intermediate sub-arithmetic of the parent has dimension 3 or 4, and nothing else; there is no 2-, 6- or other intermediate world.
The world is a product, not a sum. K is the tensor product of the two sectors, 12 = 3*4 (7), and its integers are exactly Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (8). The parent's discrete structure is built from the two sectors' lattices and nothing else.
The parent's geometry is the product of space's and spacetime's. The trace form of K has type (7,5) (10), and it is the tensor product of the sectors' own forms (PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014): (2,1) (x) (3,1), with 2*3 + 1*1 = 7 and 2*1 + 1*3 = 5. On the quartic sector the form is 3 times spacetime's own, of Lorentzian type (3,1); on the cubic sector, 4 times space's, of type (2,1) (13). The one time direction is not put in by hand: it is what the parent's form is on spacetime.
All of the parent's asymmetry between space and time is spacetime's. The parent's excess of positive over negative directions, 7 - 5 = 2, is exactly spacetime's 3 - 1 = 2. The eight dimensions orthogonal to spacetime are perfectly balanced, four positive and four negative (5, 13).
Both sectors are recovered from the parent. The relative traces, divided by the relative degrees [K:Q(rho)] = 4 and [K:Q(Q)] = 3, are the orthogonal projections onto the sectors (5), and the traces themselves carry the parent's lattice onto Z[rho] and Z[Q] (12). Every element of space and of spacetime is the shadow of an element of the parent.
The parent is built from minimizers, and joining them creates nothing smaller. Each sector's generator is a minimizer, certified in the author's registered entries: x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1 attain the least Mahler measure above 1 among irreducible integer polynomials of degrees 3 and 4 (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); rho is the least Pisot eigenvalue of any substitution on at most three letters, the slowest settling clock (PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019), and the growth rate of the triangle group (2,3,infinity) = PGL(2,Z), the slowest of the hyperbolic triangle groups (p,q,infinity) (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000013). K is the compositum of the two minimizers, and a single number generates all of it: rho*Q, the theory's coupling ruler (15; PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000005). Minimality survives the join. No element of K other than +/-1 has a conjugate on the unit circle (17), so the parent contains no Salem number, and with Smyth's theorem every nonzero integer of K other than +/-1 has Mahler measure at least rho (18), with equality at rho itself (PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004). The 3D generator is the smallest nontrivial size in the whole twelve-dimensional arithmetic, exactly as in degree 3. In the theory, rho is the ground of minimality and therefore the ground of three-dimensional structure; joining space to spacetime keeps that ground.
The two sectors are the two sides of the Pisot boundary. rho is a Pisot number, and the Padovan substitution tiling, whose characteristic polynomial is x^3 - x - 1, is a regular model set with pure-point diffraction (Baake and Grimm 2020): the ordered, classical sector. It is handed, the arrow of time: its tiling flow is neither mutually locally derivable from nor topologically conjugate to its mirror image (Gaehler 2026, Example 10 and Remark 7, where the Padovan rule is varrho_R after renaming a <-> c), and in the factor language the author's registered entries PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006, PALOMAR-2026-09-04-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000019 certify it: ca occurs and ac never does. Q is not Pisot (PALOMAR-2026-09-01-000012), and every primitive self-similar tiling of the line with expansion Q has no non-trivial pure-point spectrum (Solomyak 1997): the quantum sector, which cannot settle on a line. This is the arithmetic of a quasicrystal (superspace crystallography: de Wolff 1974; Janner and Janssen 1977; cut-and-project: de Bruijn 1981; Kramer and Neri 1984; Duneau and Katz 1985; Elser 1986): a higher-dimensional lattice, O_K in R^2 x C^5, from which the sector lattices are recovered by the traces (12).

records.doc:

records.doc:

records.doc:

Taussky 1968): the trace form Tr_{K/Q}(x^2) of a number field K has type (r1 + r2, r2), and is positive definite iff K is totally real; (3) the places of a linearly disjoint compositum L = K1 K2: r1(L) = r1(K1) r1(K2) and 2 r2(L) = [K1:Q][K2:Q] - r1(K1) r1(K2); (4) the signed discriminant of such a compositum with coprime discriminants, d_L = d_{K1}^[K2:Q] d_{K2}^[K1:Q], the sign included; (5) the trace projection [E:F]^-1 Tr_{E/F} onto a subfield F, the orthogonal decomposition E = F + F^perp for Tr_{E/Q}(xy) with F^perp = ker Tr_{E/F}, the restriction of the trace form of E to F as [E:F] times the trace form of F, and the type (r1(E) + r2(E) - r1(F) - r2(F), r2(E) - r2(F)) of its restriction to ker Tr_{E/F}; (6) the squarefree-discriminant criterion (a textbook exercise). records.name: CategoryGame.exists_jointPlay
records.entry_name: Banach–Mazur determinacy for Baire-property targets
records.doc: For any complete metric space and any target set with the property of Baire, the Banach–Mazur category game is determined: the first player has a winning full-history strategy exactly when the target is nonmeagre, and the second exactly when it is meagre. A win for the first player means one target point lies in every move. The proof constructs meagre-target avoidance without metric assumptions and shrinking closed-trap target forcing in complete metric spaces; it proves actual joint-play existence and excludes simultaneous winners. Empty spaces and equal nested moves are explicit. This is classical mathematics, with no novelty or general determinacy claim.

records.name: Submission.truncRadical_classical_tendsto
records.entry_name: RamanujanNestedRadicals: convergence and exact values of Ramanujan-type nested radicals
records.doc: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the results of the author's paper "Nested Radicals of Ramanujan's Type with Arbitrary Coefficient Sequences" (Flamandzki, 2026). For a coefficient sequence a : N -> R, the radical of depth d is built by the recursion R_k = sqrt(1 + a_k R_{k+1}) from a seed; `Submission.rollUp a T d` is the depth-d truncation with seed T and `Submission.truncRadical a d` uses the seed 1. For a root order n >= 2 the square root is replaced by the n-th root (`Submission.rollUpN`) and, for the classical unbounded family, by the signed recursion with radicand (-1)^n + a_k R_{k+1} (`Submission.rollUpNS`), whose coefficients are a_k = altSum n (N + k - 1) for the alternating polynomial altSum n x = x^(n-1) - x^(n-2) + ... +- 1. Four statements are submitted: (1) for real N >= 2 and a_k = N + k - 2 the square-root truncations converge to exactly N (for N = 3 this is Ramanujan's radical; the statement is known, see the sources, and is the base case); (2) for every root order n >= 2, both parities, the truncations of the signed family converge to exactly N, which is not treated in the sources listed below (the only place where parity enters is the sign (-1)^n); (3) an arbitrary-profile theorem: if R_k >= 1 and the coefficients are the ones for which R satisfies the recursion exactly, R_k^n = 1 + a_k R_{k+1}, then the depth-d truncation with seed 1 satisfies 0 <= R_1 - T_d <= R_1 prod_{j<d} (1 - 1/R_j), and it converges to exactly R_1 whenever the sum of 1/R_k diverges (it contains every constant profile and the classical family for every even n, with an explicit rate; it is not stated in version 2 of the paper; version 3 states it). The development (`RamanujanNested/`, 24 modules) contains further results that are not advertised in `Challenge.lean`: boundedness and monotonicity, controlled negative coefficients, the inverse construction, the closed-form identity chain for every n, the constant-coefficient exact-target radical for every n, an oscillatory family, and existence of a limit for linear and prime coefficient families at every root order. The paper's numerical tables, algorithms as running code, and informal discussion are not formalized. Zero sorries; depends only on the three standard Lean axioms.

records.name: InducedRegular.main_result
records.entry_name: Induced Erdős–Sauer: an n log log n bound
records.doc: We formalize in Lean an O_k(n log log n) bound for the induced Erdős–Sauer problem. For every fixed integer k >= 3, there is a constant C_k > 0 such that every finite simple graph on n >= 1 vertices with more than C_k n log(log(4n)) edges contains a nonempty induced k-regular subgraph. The result is unconditional, and the constants depending on k are not optimized.

records.name: Erdos249257.ExternalVerification257ReciprocalSupport.irrational_supportPowerSeries_of_summable_reciprocal
records.entry_name: Erdős #257: irrationality for every reciprocal-summable support and every integer base
records.doc: For every infinite set A of exponents whose reciprocal sum converges and every integer base b at least two, the series with terms 1/(b^a - 1) supported on A is irrational. The theorem settles the whole reciprocal-summable support regime at once and uniformly in the base, with no pairwise-coprimality, periodicity, density or powerful-support hypothesis, and with the zero exponent normalised to zero by real division. Any counterexample to the universal Erdős Problem 257 must therefore be supported on a set whose reciprocal sum diverges. The mechanism produces close returns of shifted binary support atoms from an LCM-prefix orbit-mean argument, transfers them to every radix through a uniform pointwise inequality bounding the base-b atom displacement by twice the binary one, and closes with an exact radix integer orbit. Erdős proved the pairwise-coprime case at base two and stated that pairwise coprimality can be removed by a more complicated argument without printing that argument; the base-two proof here is an independent reconstruction, the passage to every integer base is a local strengthening, and no theorem-priority claim is made and no identification with Erdős's omitted argument is asserted. The audience is analytic number theorists working on irrationality of Mersenne-type reciprocal subseries. Reciprocal-divergent supports are untouched, so the universal Erdős Problem 257 remains open.

records.name: Erdos249257.ExternalVerification269ThreePrimeStructure.smoothPrefixLcm_eq_threePrimeHeight
records.entry_name: Erdős #269: exact three-prime running-LCM identity and infinite kernel rank
records.doc: For pairwise distinct primes p, q, r and every nonzero x, the least common multiple of all smooth numbers p^i q^j r^k at most x equals the product of the three maximal pure prime powers below x. The reciprocal-height kernel K(i,j,k) built from that identity is constant on every logarithmic cell, and the first m positive jump values across the three prime channels number exactly 3m. Every finite exponent box sums to the height-fibre normal form, the sum over genuine running-LCM heights of the fibre cardinality divided by the height, and a multiplicative shell of width factor r inside a sorted exponent budget j satisfies 9 times its cardinality at most (j+3)^2. For every order n there are injective index families giving a nonsingular n by n minor of K uniformly in the remaining exponent layer, so K has infinite rank and no finite separable representation K(i,j,k) = sum over l < d of f_l(i) G_l(j,k) exists for any d. The smallest 2,3,5 rectangle has determinant exactly -1/15. Three distinct primes keep the three logarithm floors independent, which is what makes the running-LCM identity exact and the minors nonsingular in every order, and it removes every method that would evaluate the three-prime sum by finitely many separated factors. Priority for the three-prime structure has not been established, none of the seven theorems yields irrationality or transcendence, and Erdős #269 remains open.

records.entry_name: Erdős problem #257: all base irrationality of the reciprocal Mersenne subseries for every infinite reciprocal summable support, with weighted mass and positive cover extensions, achievement set geometry, and exact greedy membership criteria
records.doc:
Erdős problem 257 asks whether the sum over a in A of 1/(2^a - 1) is irrational for every infinite set A of positive integers. The principal theorem compared here settles the whole reciprocal summable regime at every integer base: if A is infinite and the sum over a in A of 1/a converges, then the sum over a in A of 1/(b^a - 1) is irrational for every integer b at least 2 (ReciprocalSupport.irrational_supportPowerSeries_of_summable_reciprocal). No pairwise coprimality, periodicity, density, or powerful support hypothesis appears. Paul Erdős printed the pairwise coprime case of exactly this statement, at every integer base, in 1968, and stated there that pairwise coprimality can be removed by a longer argument he did not print. The theorem compared here is that stated extension, proved independently. No priority over Erdős is claimed and no identification with his omitted argument is asserted. The consequence for the parent problem is a boundary condition: any infinite support witnessing a counterexample has divergent reciprocal sum. Erdős problem 257 remains open.
The readers are number theorists working on irrationality for Lambert type and reciprocal Mersenne series, and analysts who study subsum sets of convergent series. Erdős (1948) proved irrationality of the full support value at every integer base; Erdős (1968) proved the pairwise coprime reciprocal summable case; Duverney and Tachiya (2019) treated the squarefree support at every base 2^j; Tao and Teravainen proved the prime support case at base two. Duverney and Tachiya record the Erdős and Graham conjecture that the sum is irrational for every increasing sequence of exponents and describe their corollary as support for it. Each covers one distinguished family; none covers an arbitrary reciprocal summable support, nor the reciprocal divergent supports below.
Three theorems state sufficient criteria that do not ask for reciprocal summability. Write h(a) for the P part of a at a finite nonempty prime set P. DivisibilityWeightedSupport.divisibilityWeightedClaim has two clauses: convergence of the sum over a in A of h(a)/(a(b^h(a) - 1)) at a fixed base b at least 2, for infinite A avoiding 0, gives irrationality at that base; the same weighted mass at base two on a host H avoiding 0 gives irrationality at every integer base at least 2 for every infinite subset of H. VariableExponentCover.strengthenedPositiveCoverClaim gives that hereditary all base conclusion for every infinite subset of the host of a positive fractional divisor cover of convergent one inverse power cost, and MixedWeightedCover.mixedSupportClaim combines the two criteria on one observation scale. LiteralWeightedCover.exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host makes the weighted enlargement strict: a weighted host of divergent reciprocal mass admitting no strengthened cover, whose infinite subsets are irrational at every integer base at least 2. DyadicObservationSummability records dyadic averaging estimates for weighted observation masses.
FinitePeriodNoncollapse is exact finite support arithmetic: for finite nonempty F of positive exponents and integer base b at least 2, the reduced denominator of the sum over n in F of 1/(b^n - 1) is coprime to b, the order of b modulo it is exactly lcm F, and lcm F is strictly below that denominator once it is at least 2. RationalTailRigidity adds four necessary conditions on a hypothetical rational value p/(2^c v): an unbounded positive integer tail orbit with exact doubling recurrence, a sublogarithmic bound on zero windows of the divisor incidence coefficients, a reciprocal mass floor from the order of 2 modulo an odd reduced denominator when the reciprocals are summable, and a dyadic mass alternative. None contradicts a rational value. BooleanMobiusCarry gives exact coordinates: for an integer p and a positive natural q, a support avoiding 0 with some positive element and base two value p/q exists precisely when a positive square root bounded integer carry has Boolean Moebius normalised quotient. That characterisation permits finite supports, so it excludes no rational value.
AchievementSetGeometry and FairCoding describe the set of all subsums of that series at base two. For every set J of allowed digit positions the supported coding map is injective with compact nowhere dense range, the range is perfect when J is infinite, and the Lebesgue measure obeys an exact dichotomy: 2^(-|F|) when the omitted positions form a finite set F, and zero when infinitely many are omitted. When 0 is not in J and the value coded by J read as exponents is rational, the supported set is Lebesgue null, which closes positive measure selection over a rational fibre. The fair product measure on digit strings pushes forward to Lebesgue measure restricted to the achievement set, and the preimage of the rationals is null. Perfectness and nowhere density of subsum sets are classical after Kakeya (1914), and Kovac and Tao record the fixed base Cantor structure; the measure dichotomy and the rational fibre null theorem are the additions.
Six families give exact membership criteria for that set. GeneralRepairCriterion replaces a quantifier over supports by a pointwise inequality on one integer sequence: a nonnegative real lies in the set exactly when its greedy defect fails to increase at cofinally many scales, and when it fails to increase inside every window that starts at K and has width 2 times the integer square root of K plus 12. ScaledGreedyTrap identifies the set with the nonnegative reals whose scaled greedy remainder stays strictly below the barrier 2 at every scale. RationalMembership characterises a nonnegative rational target by infinitude of its skipped greedy ranks; PositiveSkipEquivalence and FourNinthsRepairWindows give the criteria at 1/2 and at 4/9; TwentyOneFatalBranch reduces membership of 1/21 to excluding one explicit fatal aligned branch. These are exact reformulations; they decide no target.
TerminalScaledVanishing and ActualUpperSuccessor state conditional refutations of the universal assertion: an unconstructed terminal scaled vanishing sequence of finite Boolean support words, or an unconstructed realised upper run lower envelope, each produces an infinite support of value exactly 1/2. Neither theorem places 1/2 in the achievement set.
Irrationality for an arbitrary infinite support is not proved, the memberships of 1/2, 4/9 and 1/21 are not decided, and the parent problem remains open.

records.name: PalomarCorpus.E249.CompleteKernelBases.displayed_all_base_kernel
records.entry_name: All-base bases and integral relations for the totient kernel
records.doc: For every integer base k at least two and depth e at least one, the rational span of the sections n ↦ φ(k^j n+r) through level e has dimension k^e+1. An explicit retained family is a basis, every omitted section is an integer multiple of a retained section, and these reductions form a basis for all integral relations, with rank Σ_(1≤j<e) k^j. The entry also gives the full dyadic basis and an affine independence theorem. The retained positive residues satisfy k ∤ r, a weaker condition than gcd(k,r)=1. Martin’s earlier theorem already implies affine independence, and Coons proved non-k-regularity; the exact finite-level basis and integral normal form are the contribution here. This configuration does not prove irrationality of Σ φ(n)2^(-n). The retained family includes φ(n), φ(kn), and all positive residues r with k ∤ r at every level through e. The integral relations are indexed by omitted channels, each with coefficient one at its own channel, which supplies uniqueness over Z.

records.name: SidonSubmission.weak_sidon_limit
records.entry_name: Selected Sidon subset theorems of Ma–Tang (partial paper formalization)
records.doc: Lean 4 proofs of the exact largest-Sidon-subset guarantee g(n)=ceil((n+1)/2) for finite weak Sidon sets, its asymptotic density 1/2, convergence and the optimal-constant characterization for finite (4,5)-sets, and the upper bound cStar<=4/7. The project also proves the finite three-uniform transversal bound 4tau<=n+m used in the exact guarantee. This is a partial formalization of Ma–Tang, arXiv:2602.23282v2: Theorem5.3 and the lower9/17 bound in Theorem1.6 remain unproved.

records.name: SymplecticStaffordChallenge.universalStatement
records.entry_name: Symplectic Stafford: the affine same-divisor theorem
records.doc: Let k be a field of characteristic zero and U a simple, infinite-dimensional k-algebra with an exhaustive nonnegative multiplicative filtration by finite-dimensional k-subspaces. Suppose F_0 U = k and the associated graded algebra is a commutative affine domain of finite Krull dimension. Then for every nonzero d, a in U and every B in U there exist H, R, S in U such that 1 = dR + (B + Ha)dS. The Lean 4 development proves this theorem, its left-handed form, and module generation, stable range and cancellation results for U.

records.name: LowerUpperBounds.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Lower and Upper Bounds for Glauber Dynamics from Typical States of the Low-Temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick Model
records.doc: Lean formalization of five manuscript result groups: Theorems 1.1, 1.3, and 1.6, and Corollaries 1.2 and 1.7. The barrier covers both clocks and every fixed threshold below one half, with exponent 7/30. The upper bound is the continuous-time statement for every fixed exponent saving between zero and one quarter. The fluctuation exponents and mean-bias lower bound have their stated positive exponent slack. Corollary 1.7 also explicitly concludes convergence of the finite-volume counting pressures to the limiting pressure. The manuscript and exact scope are included.

The barrier covers both clocks and every fixed threshold below one half, with exponent 7/30. The upper bound is the continuous-time statement for every fixed exponent saving between zero and one quarter. The fluctuation exponents and mean-bias lower bound have their stated positive exponent slack. Corollary 1.7 also explicitly concludes convergence of the finite-volume counting pressures to the limiting pressure. The manuscript and exact scope are included.

records.name: StrongChoquet.exists_legalPlay
records.entry_name: The strong Choquet characterization of Polish spaces
records.doc: For every second-countable metrizable topological space, the second player has a winning full-history strong Choquet strategy if and only if the topology admits a complete metric, equivalently if and only if the space is Polish. Moves include a marked point which every response must retain. The difficult converse constructs a coherent countable response tree, proves the embedded image is Gδ, and transfers complete metrizability from the metric completion. Supporting results prove complete-metric winning strategies without second countability, complete metrizability of Gδ subsets of arbitrary complete metric spaces, actual legal-play existence and explicit empty-space behavior. This is classical mathematics; no novelty or priority is claimed.

records.name: LeanLab.Romanov.romanov
records.entry_name: Romanov's theorem: the integers of the form p + 2^k have positive lower density, with Erdős' complement, after Romanov 1934 and Erdős 1950
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of N. P. Romanov, Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie, Math. Ann. 109, 1934: the integers p + 2^k, p prime, have positive lower density, for k >= 0 and for k >= 1. With it, the result of P. Erdős, On integers of the form 2^k + p and some related problems, Summa Brasil. Math. 2, 1950: by a covering system, every 119477317 + 346729110 t is odd and is not p + 2^k, so the odd numbers that are not of that form also have positive lower density. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.

records.name: LeanLab.Brun1919.brun
records.entry_name: Brun's theorem: the sum of the reciprocals of the twin primes converges, after Brun 1919, with the twin prime upper bound and every even gap
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of the theorem of V. Brun, La série 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 + 1/13 + ... où les dénominateurs sont nombres premiers jumeaux est convergente ou finie, Bull. Sci. Math. 43, 1919: the sum of the reciprocals of p and of p + 2 over the primes p with p + 2 prime converges. This is a sorry-free proof of a statement that lean-eval lists as a challenge, brun_constant_converges, proved here in the exact lean-eval form as well. With it, the twin prime upper bound, at most C N / log^2 N twin primes below N, which is stronger than the bound of Brun's paper; the same convergence for prime pairs p, p + h with any even gap h; a bound for those pairs with one constant for every gap; and its average over gaps. The bounds come from the Selberg sieve, ported from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd, not from Brun's sieve. Binary Goldbach and the twin prime conjecture are open and are not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.

records.name: TPerfect.Palomar.fiftyColor
records.entry_name: The 50-color theorem for t-perfect graphs
records.doc: A Lean proof that every finite t-perfect graph is 50-colorable. Here t-perfection means equality between the stable set polytope and the polytope described by coordinate, edge, and odd-cycle inequalities.

records.name: LeanLab.SchnirelmannGoldbach.S4_schnirelmann_pos
records.entry_name: Schnirelmann's theorem: every integer n >= 2 is a sum of at most 30772 primes, after Schnirelmann 1933
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of L. Schnirelmann, Über additive Eigenschaften von Zahlen, Math. Ann. 107, 1933: the set of 0, 1 and the sums of two primes has positive Schnirelmann density, and so every integer n >= 2 is a sum of a bounded number of primes. The proof also gives an explicit bound: every n >= 2 is a sum of at most 30772 primes. Mathlib's file Mathlib/Combinatorics/Schnirelmann.lean lists the proof of Schnirelmann's theorem as a TODO; this entry gives it, for Mathlib's schnirelmannDensity, with an explicit constant. The constant 30772 is far weaker than the best known ones: Ramaré 1995 showed that every n >= 2 is a sum of at most 7 primes, and Helfgott's ternary Goldbach theorem gives at most 4. The point is a complete formal version of Schnirelmann's argument with every constant explicit. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.

records.name: WeightedMIS.Spec.main_claim
records.entry_name: An XP Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Independent Set in Embedded Graphs, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1 of "Maximum-weight independent set in embedded graphs parameterized by Euler genus and number of odd faces" (forthcoming), with a provably correct implementation of the algorithm as one fixed program for an explicit sixteen-register pointer machine. Lean proves that for every graph drawn in a closed surface of Euler genus gamma whose complement has k regions of odd total boundary length, and all rational vertex weights, the program outputs a maximum-weight independent set within f(gamma + k) * N^(D(gamma, k) + C) * (L + 1)^b bit operations, with D(gamma, k) = max {0, gamma + k - 2, gamma - 1}, improved to max {0, gamma + k - 2} on orientable surfaces; f is an explicit computable function and C, b are absolute constants. Surfaces are represented by finite combinatorial flag maps; disconnected and noncellular drawings, loops, multiple edges, isolated vertices and negative weights are covered. The cost is a logarithmic bit-cost measure including an explicit stack simulation of recursive calls. The proofs use exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: not_RamanujanCongruence_verbose
records.entry_name: Ramanujan congruences for the partition function
records.doc: A Lean formalization of modular forms over coefficient subrings of the complex numbers, their coefficientwise reductions modulo ring homomorphisms,  and a proof classifying the Ramanujan congruences for the partition function following an argument from Ahlgren and Boylan.  The recorded results prove Ramanujan's congruences modulo 5, 7, and 11  as well as the fact there there are no other such examples. The proof develops modular forms modulo a prime, filtration, and theta and U operators, using the arguments of Ahlgren–Boylan, Kiming–Olsson, and Swinnerton-Dyer.

records.name: PlanarCycles.Lienard.SexticSix.sextic_six_limit_cycles
records.entry_name: Classical Liénard equations of degree n ≥ 6 can have floor((n−1)/2)+4 limit cycles
records.doc: For the classical Liénard system dx/dt = y − F(x), dy/dt = −x, every polynomial in an explicit coefficient box of radius 10^−40 around a rational sextic has at least six limit cycles. For every integer n ≥ 6, a real polynomial of degree exactly n with F(0) = 0 is shown to have at least floor((n − 1)/2) + 4 limit cycles. An explicit rational polynomial of degree seven, obtained by adding 10^−41 x^7 to the sextic, has at least seven limit cycles. records.name: UniversalGroup.exists_two_generator_thirteen_relator_universal_group
records.entry_name: A universal group with thirteen relators
records.doc: Lean 4 proof that there exists a presentation with two generators and thirteen relators whose group contains an isomorphic copy of every finitely presented group. The construction combines a universal finitely presented input, positive preparation, word recognition, a six-generator nineteen-relator host, and a final HNN compression.

records.name: Controller.Cost.CriticalSets.cycle_complete
records.entry_name: Critical recovery, query lower bounds and binary-native width
records.doc: Critical detecting-set counts, physical test-list and black-box query lower bounds, and critical-set and cycle recovery through a fixed source-reading program. Primal/incidence treewidth bounds concern specification and complete binary-expanded native CNF graphs; a conditional cover-layout theorem bounds treewidth, net-cutwidth and block width. Strong and deletion backdoors into Horn, renamable-Horn and two-CNF have cardinality at least the bus count for both native and specification formulas.

records.doc: Critical detecting-set counts, physical test-list and black-box query lower bounds, and critical-set and cycle recovery through a fixed source-reading program. Primal/incidence treewidth bounds concern specification and complete binary-expanded native CNF graphs; a conditional cover-layout theorem bounds treewidth, net-cutwidth and block width. Strong and deletion backdoors into Horn, renamable-Horn and two-CNF have cardinality at least the bus count for both native and specification formulas.

records.name: GridHam.ips_characterization
records.entry_name: Hamiltonian paths in rectangular grid graphs (Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter)
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof of the characterization of Hamiltonian paths in rectangular grid graphs by Itai, Papadimitriou and Szwarcfiter (1982, Theorem 3.2). For distinct vertices s and t of the width × height grid graph, a Hamiltonian path from s to t exists if and only if the problem is acceptable, that is, colour compatible (by the checkerboard colouring) and not one of the three forbidden configurations F1, F2, F3 on grids of width or height 1, 2 or 3. Necessity is proved for each forbidden case, where the paper only says "a straightforward case analysis". Sufficiency is proved by strong induction with an explicit reduction rule (strip two columns or split at a cut edge) and 596 kernel-checked base-case paths.

records.name: CCDN.Submission.affineCount_set_finite
records.entry_name: Dimension growth, polynomial in the degree (Castryck–Cluckers–Dittmann–Nguyen)
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalisation of the main results of Castryck, Cluckers, Dittmann and Nguyen, "The dimension growth conjecture, polynomial in the degree and without logarithmic factors" (Algebra & Number Theory 14, 2020), incorporating the authors' 2026 addenda. It proves uniform bounds, polynomial in the degree, for the number of rational points of bounded height on varieties over Q. The bounds are: projective dimension growth N(X,B) ≤ C(n) d^(2n²+5n−5) B^dim X for integral X ⊆ P^n of degree d ≥ 5 (Theorem 1); N(X,B) ≤ C(n) d⁴ B^(2/d) for integral projective curves (Theorem 2); N_aff(X,B) ≤ C(n) d³ B^(1/d)(log B + d) for integral affine curves (Theorem 3); and C(N) d^(3N+9) B^(N−2) for affine hypersurfaces whose top-degree form is absolutely irreducible (Theorem 4). It also proves the lower-bound construction d² B^(2/d)/5 (Proposition 5), and the 2-torsion bound h₂(K) ≤ C(n) |disc K|^(1/2−1/(2n)) (log |disc K|)^(1−n mod 2) for all number fields of degree n ≥ 3 (Theorem 6). Degree and dimension are defined through Hilbert functions of the coordinate ring. Every constant depends only on the ambient dimension or field degree. The proofs construct the paper's determinant-method, projection and counting arguments in full. They include corrected versions of several intermediate lemmas whose printed forms are false.

records.name: CountingSTS.N_le_D
records.entry_name: Counting Steiner triple systems: Wilson (1974) and Linial–Luria (2013)
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of R. M. Wilson's "Nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems" (inequality (2.1), Theorems 1–4, Lemmas 3–5, including the exact numbers of Latin squares of orders 6, 7 and 8 and the bounds N(19) ≥ 2450, N(21) ≥ 2160980, N(25) ≥ 163929929318400) and of N. Linial and Z. Luria's "An upper bound on the number of Steiner triple systems" (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 with explicit error terms). Version 2 adds a proof of the van der Waerden permanent theorem (Egorychev, Falikman), following Gurvits's proof as simplified by Laurent and Schrijver. The parts of Wilson's Theorems 2 and 3 that rely on it are stated both as implications from the hypothesis vdWPC, as in the paper, and unconditionally (theorem2_full, theorem3_full). Finite computations are kernel-checked certificates (no native_decide). Mathlib does not contain these results.

records.name: Lsbgcd.gcd_correct
records.entry_name: Analysis of a left-shift binary GCD algorithm (Shallit–Sorenson 1994), with a proof of its sum-of-squares conjecture
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 formalization of Jeffrey Shallit and Jonathan Sorenson, "Analysis of a Left-Shift Binary GCD Algorithm" (J. Symbolic Computation 17, 1994). LSBGCD replaces (u, v) by v and the distance from u to the nearer of the shifted multiples 2^e v and 2^(e+1) v, where 2^e v ≤ u < 2^(e+1) v. The formalization proves that the algorithm computes the gcd, and proves Theorem 1.1: for every n, the lexicographically least ordered input taking exactly n iterations, its six closed forms in powers of 2 ± √3, and the order-16 linear recurrence satisfied by both coordinates. It proves in full generality Ramharter's theorem on continuant-minimising permutations (Theorem 5.1, quoted in the paper from Ramharter 1983), for arbitrary positive digits with repetition and with uniqueness up to reversal. It also proves the paper's binary minimiser classification (Theorem 5.2) and the sharp logarithmic iteration bound of §7 with an explicit additive constant. In addition it proves the sum-of-squares conjecture stated without proof at the end of §6: for n ≥ 2, among ordered positive inputs taking exactly n iterations, u² + v² is uniquely minimised by consecutive terms of the printed recurrence, which are denominators of convergents to √3. A limited literature search found no earlier proof of this conjecture, but its novelty has not been established.

The formalization proves that the algorithm computes the gcd, and proves Theorem 1.1: for every n, the lexicographically least ordered input taking exactly n iterations, its six closed forms in powers of 2 ± √3, and the order-16 linear recurrence satisfied by both coordinates. It proves in full generality Ramharter's theorem on continuant-minimising permutations (Theorem 5.1, quoted in the paper from Ramharter 1983), for arbitrary positive digits with repetition and with uniqueness up to reversal. It also proves the paper's binary minimiser classification (Theorem 5.2) and the sharp logarithmic iteration bound of §7 with an explicit additive constant. In addition it proves the sum-of-squares conjecture stated without proof at the end of §6: for n ≥ 2, among ordered positive inputs taking exactly n iterations, u² + v² is uniquely minimised by consecutive terms of the printed recurrence, which are denominators of convergents to √3. A limited literature search found no earlier proof of this conjecture, but its novelty has not been established.

records.name: PottsContinuity.isPottsCriticalPoint_unique
records.entry_name: Continuity of the phase transition for planar random-cluster and Potts models with 1 <= q <= 4 (Theorems 1, 2 and 3)
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorems 1, 2 and 3 of Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius and Tassion (arXiv:1505.04159v1). Theorem 3: for the random-cluster model on the square lattice with any real cluster weight q >= 1, at its critical point p_c, the following are equivalent: the origin lies in an infinite cluster with probability 0 under the wired measure; equality of the free and wired measures; infinite susceptibility of the free measure; sub-exponential decay of the free one-arm probability; and the RSW bound for free boundary conditions at distance n. Theorem 2: for 1 <= q <= 4 the wired measure at p_c gives probability 0 to the origin lying in an infinite cluster. Theorem 1: for the q-state Potts model with q = 2, 3, 4, the monochromatic Gibbs measure at beta_c gives its own colour at the origin probability exactly 1/q, so the phase transition is continuous. The critical points are the genuine phase-transition thresholds, whose existence the theorems assert; four further theorems prove that these critical points and the infinite-volume measures are unique; beyond this statement surface, the development also proves p_c = sqrt(q)/(1 + sqrt q) for every q >= 1 (PottsContinuity.BD12.isRCCriticalPoint_sqrt) and beta_c = log(1 + sqrt q) for every integer q >= 2 (PottsContinuity.Thm1.isPottsCriticalPoint_log_sqrt); these identifications are not checked by Comparator. The infinite-volume measures are limits along every exhaustion of the lattice, and their existence and uniqueness are proved. The external results that the paper cites and the proof uses (the value of p_c and the crossing estimates of Beffara-Duminil-Copin, the contour identity of the parafermionic observable in the form used in Section 4 of the paper, Theorem 4 of the paper, the Edwards-Sokal coupling, FKG and comparison inequalities, the domain Markov property, planar duality and topology) are proved here or taken from Mathlib; the Jordan-Schoenflies theorem and Brouwer's fixed-point theorem come from vendored libraries, and circle-degree and Jordan-curve facts from the Tau Ceti library. The only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: Combinatorics.Line.exists_mono_of_ack_le'
records.entry_name: Shelah's bound for the Hales–Jewett numbers
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of Shelah's proof of the Hales–Jewett theorem. For k ≥ 1 letters and r colors, every coloring with r colors of the words of length n over k letters has a monochromatic combinatorial line when n is at least the Ackermann function at level 5 and argument 2k + r.

records.name: IwaniecLinearSieve.iwaniecBound
records.entry_name: Iwaniec's linear sieve at the sifting limit and Jacobsthal's problem
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of H. Iwaniec, "On the error term in the linear sieve" (Acta Arith. 19, 1971) and "On the problem of Jacobsthal" (Demonstratio Math. 11, 1978). The headline result is Iwaniec's bound for Jacobsthal's problem: if m consecutive integers are each divisible by one of r ≥ 2 given primes, then m ≤ C (r log r)² for an absolute constant C. More strongly, every interval of length c ∏ (1 − 1/q)⁻¹ r² log r contains at least r² integers coprime to r given primes. Both the Theorem and the Corollary of the 1978 paper are proved, together with its Lemma 1 (the shifted sieve, both bounds) and Lemma 2. The 1971 paper is formalized in full: the Rosser–Iwaniec linear sieve at the sifting limit with general modulus k and arbitrary finite sequences (§2); the sieve functions f, F and the majorants 𝔐, 𝔚 defined by delay-differential equations, including F(3) = 2e^γ − 3 and the asymptotics of 𝔐 (§3); the main term with error O(1/log y) and support of size O(y / log² y) (§4, Theorems 4 and 5); and Theorem 1 with its Corollary, Theorem 2 (C₀(r) ≪ r² log² r) and Theorem 3 (§5). The prime number theorem with de la Vallée Poussin error term and Mertens' theorems come from a vendored copy of PrimeNumberTheoremAnd.

records.name: LeanLab.HardyLittlewood1923.theoremB
records.entry_name: Sums of primes, after Hardy and Littlewood 1923, Partitio Numerorum III, Theorems B to F proved without Hypothesis R
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof, with no hypothesis, of Theorems B, C, D, E and F of G. H. Hardy and J. E. Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III, Acta Math. 44, 1923. Hardy and Littlewood proved these theorems on their Hypothesis R, a form of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions; here they are proved unconditionally, from Vinogradov's estimate for exponential sums over primes and the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, so the argument is not Hardy and Littlewood's own for Theorems B, D and E. Formalized: Theorem B, the asymptotic for the weighted count nu_r of n as an ordered sum of r primes, for every r at least 3 and n of the parity of r, with the singular series written as the paper's product over the odd primes dividing n, and nu_r of n is o of n^{r-1} for unlike parity; Theorem C, N_r of n is asymptotic to nu_r of n over log^r n; Theorem D, the ternary asymptotic with the constant C_3 and every large odd number a sum of three odd primes; Theorem E, the asymptotic for four odd primes, every large even number a sum of four odd primes, one of which may be assigned; and Theorem F, that an asymptotic of Conjecture A's shape for binary Goldbach can only carry the constant 2 C_2, together with a check that the printed formula 4.23 has a misprint. Theorem A of the paper is not formalized. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem; binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. records.doc: Conditional on RH: a sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Theorem 2 of D. A. Goldston and L. Yang, The average number of Goldbach representations, arXiv 1601.06902, in Prime numbers and representation theory, Science Press 2017. With G(n) the sum over m1 + m2 = n of Lambda(m1) Lambda(m2), Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, taken as an explicit hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom, implies that the sum over n <= N of 1 - n/N times G(n) equals N^2/6 - 2 times the sum over nontrivial zeros rho of N^{rho+1} divided by rho times rho+1 times rho+2, plus O(N), for N >= 2. records.entry_name: Mann's alpha plus beta theorem for Schnirelmann density, after Mann 1942
records.doc: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of H. B. Mann, A proof of the fundamental theorem on the density of sums of sets of positive integers, Ann. of Math. 43, 1942: for sets A and B of natural numbers that contain 0, the Schnirelmann density of A + B is at least the minimum of 1 and sigma A + sigma B. It is stated for Mathlib's own schnirelmannDensity and Mathlib's pointwise sum of sets, so the Challenge restates no density definition, and it is also proved for any finite number of sets. This fills a Mathlib TODO: Mathlib/Combinatorics/Schnirelmann.lean lists Mann's theorem as not yet proved. Soc. 140 2012, 795 to 804. With G(n) the sum over m1 + m2 = n of Lambda(m1) Lambda(m2), Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, taken as an explicit hypothesis of the theorem and never as an axiom, implies that the sum over n <= N of G(n) equals N^2/2 - 2 times the sum over nontrivial zeros rho of N^{rho+1} divided by rho times rho+1, plus O(N log^3 N), for N >= 2. records.name: LeanLab.PNTPort.BVMax.bombieriVinogradovMax
records.entry_name: The Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem, Bombieri 1965 and A. I. Vinogradov 1965, classical form with the maximum over y <= x
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem in its classical form: for every A > 0 there is B > 0 such that the sum over q <= x^{1/2} (log x)^{-B} of the maximum over y <= x and over reduced residues a mod q of |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| is << x (log x)^{-A}. The same form is proved for theta(y; q, a), for pi(y; q, a) against liD(y)/phi(q) with liD(y) the sum of 1/log n over 2 <= n <= y, and for pi(y; q, a) against pi(y)/phi(q), the level of distribution 1/2 input of sieve methods. The proof runs from a zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions and Siegel's theorem through the Siegel-Walfisz theorem, the multiplicative large sieve and Vaughan's identity; all constants are ineffective, as in the papers. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were checked against the literature by AI reviewers and are offered for human audit.

records.name: ETSHTS.clm0107_exact
records.entry_name: Noncrossing Two-Nearest-Predecessor Orders on Nearly Circular Ellipses
records.doc: We prove a uniform all-cardinality existence theorem for noncrossing chronological two-nearest-predecessor graphs on sufficiently near-circular ellipses. Put R = sqrt(2/sin(2*pi/5) - 1). For every ellipse with semiaxes a >= b > 0 and a/b <= R, and every finite set of at least three distinct boundary sites, there is an order starting with a triangle in which every subsequent site is joined to exactly its two Euclidean-nearest earlier sites. All edges persist, and no two independent edges properly cross. Cartesian-lexicographic order resolves equal-distance predecessor ties. The sufficient ratio bound includes equality, all finite cardinalities and arbitrarily close distinct sites. The interest lies in planarity despite compulsory distance-ranked edges: unlike conventional convex-polygon triangulation, the two incoming edges cannot be chosen just to avoid crossings. The constructive proof uses recursive metric-ear deletion; the accompanying manuscript also gives an exact-real comparison-model algorithm, whose complexity is not a separately compared Lean claim. The bound is not claimed to be sharp; historical priority remains unestablished. The repository also contains formally proved supporting geometry and a concrete noncircular corollary, but these are not submitted as independent research results in the selected Comparator configuration.

records.name: LeanLab.PNTPort.BVMax.renyi8_fixedK
records.entry_name: Renyi's theorem, Renyi 1948: every large even number is a prime plus a number with at most 8 prime factors
records.doc: A sorry-free Lean 4 proof of Renyi's theorem: there is N0 such that every even N >= N0 is p + m with p prime, m >= 1 and Omega of m at most 8, where Omega counts prime factors with multiplicity, as Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors does. So the theorem is proved with the explicit constant K = 8. Also proved: a lower bound e^{-36} N / 2 log^2 N for the number of primes p < N with Omega of N - p at most 8; the same two statements with the weaker K = 13000; and the K = 8 statement written with Mathlib's Nat.IsAtMostAlmostPrime. The entry also proves twin_renyi_count, a derived analogue proved in this entry by the same sieve method, a twin-prime analogue of Renyi's theorem, not a result of Renyi 1948. The proof is a Brun type block sieve with Bonferroni levels whose remainders are bounded by the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem proved in the same library; all thresholds are ineffective through Siegel's theorem. Nothing here is new mathematics: Pan has K = 4 and Chen 1973 has K = 2. Binary Goldbach is Omega of m equal to 1; it is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent; the statements were checked against the literature by AI reviewers and are offered for human audit.

records.name: RandomDifferences.szemeredi_setBernoulli_exists_avoiding_le_exp
records.entry_name: Szemerédi's theorem with random differences
records.doc: Lean 4 formalization of the main result of the preprint "Szemerédi's theorem with random differences and arithmetic Kakeya" by Gabriel Dahia (arXiv:2610.18859), a threshold for Szemerédi's theorem with random differences. For c = 1/100, k ≥ 3, δ > 0 and p ≥ C n^(-c / log log k), where C is a value of the Ackermann function depending on k and δ, a p-random set D of differences in {1, …, n} has the following property with probability at least 1 - exp(-n^(1 - c / log log k)): every subset of {1, …, n} with at least δn elements contains a k-term arithmetic progression with common difference in D. The proof uses the Green–Ruzsa construction of small sets containing a progression with every common difference, which is also formalized.

records.name: ModelSetDimension.admissibility_criterion
records.entry_name: The least physical dimension of an inflation-symmetric model set, with the cubic, quartic and degree-12 inflations of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1
records.doc:
Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, about cut-and-project schemes on a fixed integer lattice Z^iota invariant under an integer matrix A: splittings R^iota = E + H into A-invariant subspaces with Z^iota meeting H only in 0 and the projection of Z^iota to H dense in H, a window W in H (bounded, containing a relative ball), the model set Lambda(W) = {pi_E g : g in Z^iota, pi_H g in W}, and admissibility, some window with A Lambda(W) contained in Lambda(W) (inflation symmetry in Meyer's inclusion sense). The least physical dimension d(A) is the least dim E over admissible schemes. Thirteen compared theorems. (1) For every integer A, a scheme is admissible iff A is power-bounded on H; then the orbit window is a compact convex symmetric invariant window; the per-window criterion; and U(A) <= dim E, U(A) the number of eigenvalues of modulus > 1. (2) Kronecker's density criterion in cut-and-project form. (3) For every integer A with det A != 0, any chi_A: (a) d(A) is the sum over the distinct irreducible factors p of chi_A over Q of m_p u_p + c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), plus min(deg p, 2) when every root of p lies on the unit circle and r_1(p) = m_p, where m_p is the multiplicity, u_p and c_p count the roots of p of modulus > 1 and = 1, and r_1(p) = (2 dim ker p(A) - dim ker p(A)^2) / deg p (ranks over Q) is the number of Jordan blocks of size one at each root of p; (b) the value is an invariant of rational similarity; (c) the factors with all roots on the unit circle are the cyclotomic ones; and (d) for chi_A squarefree every invariant splitting is E = ker q_E(A), H = ker q_H(A) with chi_A = q_E q_H, it is admissible iff the roots of q_H lie in the closed unit disk and every irreducible rational factor of chi_A shares a root with q_E, and d(A) = U(A) + circleCount(A), counting 1 for each factor x - 1, x + 1 and 2 for each other cyclotomic factor, each with its multiplicity. (4) For det A != 0 and hyperbolic A, any chi_A and no diagonalizability: a scheme is admissible iff E contains the unstable set iff H lies in the stable set; an invariant splitting carries an admissible scheme iff E contains the unstable set; d(A) = U(A), attained only by the unstable/stable splitting. (5) For det A != 0, any chi_A: d(A) = 1 iff chi_A is irreducible with exactly one root of modulus > 1 (a real root, a Pisot or Salem number up to sign, or an integer on Z^1), or A = +-1 in any rank; in the irreducible case every admissible line is the eigenline. (6) If A^k = 1: every factor is cyclotomic and d = sum of min(deg p, 2) over the distinct factors; the same for chi_A squarefree with all roots on the unit circle; every integer matrix with chi_A = Phi_n, n >= 3 (multiplication by a primitive n-th root of unity), needs exactly a plane. (7) Jordan blocks on the circle: I_2 and the Jordan block J_2 both have chi = (x - 1)^2, for which the squarefree count of (3), with x - 1 counted twice, gives 2, but d = 1 and 2; 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) have d = 2 and 3. (8) Multiplication by rho, rho^-1, Q and theta = -Q^-1 = 1 - Q^3 on Z[rho] and Z[Q] (rho^3 = rho + 1, Q^4 = Q + 1): d = 1, 2, 3, 1. (9) On Z[rho] (x) Z[Q] (degree 12), multiplication by every alpha other than 0, +-1 is nonsingular (det != 0) and hyperbolic with d = U; for rho, theta, rho Q and Q the values are 4, 3, 5, 9. (10) rho and theta act on their unstable spaces as real scalars, and the spectral projection carries the quartic (resp. cubic) sector onto them with the Gram pairing GramRho (x) GramQ equal to that of GramQ (resp. GramRho), of types (3,1) and (2,1). (11) The scheme of Q on Z^4 with an interval window: a segment, an explicit Q-invariant model set in R^3, determinant -1/q' on E, non-real moduli, and the types (2,1) and (1,0) of the trace form on E and H. (12) A Salem witness, the companion of x^4 - x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: not hyperbolic, d = 1. (13) Every model set is a Delone set (Mathlib's Delone.DeloneSet) with uniformly discrete difference set. The mathematics of (1), (2), (4), (5) for irreducible chi_A, and (13), and of (6) for chi_A = Phi_n, is known in other formulations (Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova 2021; Kronecker, Pleasants 2000; Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton 2025, preprint; Meyer 1972, 1995; Lagarias 1999; Solomyak 2020; the classical cyclotomic model sets; Moody 1997); (1) and (4) are stated with no diagonalizability hypothesis. The scheme and model set of (11) are, in substance, instances of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova Thm 13.1 and of Harriss-Koivusalo-Walton Section 3.4, and are not new. For squarefree chi_A the count of (3) also follows from the arguments of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova (Lemma 5.1, Prop. 8.1(iii), Cor. 13.4), stated there for generic (aperiodic) schemes; the lattice-first least physical dimension was not found stated in the sources read (search completed 2026-10-20). Beyond the cited cases, the entry proves the least physical dimension for every nonsingular integer matrix (3), including what lies outside the diagonalizable class of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova: a Jordan block of size >= 2 at an eigenvalue on the unit circle counts in full (the terms c_p (m_p - r_1(p)), which vanish for diagonalizable A), and at a cyclotomic factor with such a block the blocks of size one cost nothing, the internal space being tilted into the socle of the larger blocks; the witnesses are J_2, 1 + J_2(1) and 1 + J_3(1) (7). Every admissible scheme of an A with such a block at a root of unity has Z^iota meeting E in a nonzero vector. It also proves the characterization of every admissible splitting for squarefree chi_A ((3)(d)), non-generic splittings included (its necessity half is the injectivity argument of Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Lemma 5.1), and (1) for every integer matrix and (4) for every nonsingular hyperbolic integer matrix, with no diagonalizability hypothesis; for diagonalizable A and generic schemes, the uniqueness of the minimal scheme in (4) and of the minimal physical line in (5) is immediate from Masakova-Mazac-Pelantova, Cor. 13.4. For det A != 0 and squarefree chi_A with a factor Phi_n, n not in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6}, the minimal scheme is not unique, by (3)(d). The companion matrices are multiplication by rho and Q in the power bases by definition, so Crho^i (x) CQ^j is multiplication by rho^i Q^j in the product basis. That the rho^i Q^j are a Z-basis of the ring of integers of Q(rho, Q) is statement (8) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031); that GramRho, GramQ and GramRho (x) GramQ are the Gram matrices of the trace forms in these bases is statements (8), (9) and (19) of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014, in which Q(rho) (x) Q(Q) is the field Q(rho, Q) (its (23)). These are cited, not compared. Application (cited, not a claim of the entry): In the author's Pisot Dimensional Theory, Q(rho) is the arithmetic of three-dimensional space and Q(Q) the arithmetic of four-dimensional spacetime, and their compositum K, whose integers are Z[rho] (x) Z[Q], is the parent of both (the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (stalex444/pdt-hermite-signature-compositum@5aa870e98236ba240561b798265c629df8c2d031), statements (7), (8)). A model set is the shadow of a lattice cut through a window, a standard mathematical model of a quasicrystal (Moody 2000). Read through the theory, this entry's theorems fix how many dimensions each of the theory's inflations needs to be the symmetry of one, and which ones.
Space inflates the parent through spacetime, and spacetime inflates it through space. On the parent's lattice the plastic inflation rho needs exactly four physical dimensions, and only one scheme attains four (4, 9).
